# 17 · The Festival State
Happiness as a *spent* resource: games, feasts, processions. The loop: surplus happiness
+ gold → spectacle → culture, renown, drafts. Nothing else in the game uses happiness as
an input — and Entry LIV's scarcity ruling makes that input precious, which is exactly
what makes spending it a build. Wins by: the contentment measures · The Great Games ·
the Golden Age itself.

**Tech:** none of its own — spectacle is bought, not researched; Rhetoric (III) carries the theatre if it wants a home.

## Æra I
- Buildings: Funeral Games (the existing early renown building — this theme's front door)
- Orders:
  - Festival Days — +4 happiness.
- Religion:
  - Feast Days — +1 happiness for every city that follows, and +1 more for each with a Temple.

## Æra II
- Doctrines:
  - Bread and Circuses — While your authority is positive: +3 happiness in every city. −1 gold in every city, always.
- Orders:
  - The Processions *(proposal)* — +1 culture for every 2 points of surplus happiness (cap +6). (The meter becomes a yield — the theme's first converter.)
- Wonders:
  - The Theatre of Dionysus — +1 happiness in every city with an Amphitheater · on completion, a Doctrine draft opens
- Deeds:
  - The Great Feast *(proposal, feat)* — the first empire to hold +15 surplus happiness. [remove]

## Æra III
- Orders:
  - The Grain Dole — +2 happiness in every city of 6 or more population.
  - Mandate of Heaven — The science and culture your happy cities pay rises from 10% to 15% · +1 happiness for each 200 banked faith. (shared with 03 — arguably this theme's card)
- Projects:
  - The Games *(proposal — the repeatable engine)* — a project: spend hammers and gold → +3 happiness in every city for 10 turns and a culture lump; each Games costs and pays more than the last. (The project machinery already rate-limits and refuses doubles.)
- Wonders:
  - The Circus Maximus — +1 happiness per Barracks · +4 happiness
- **The marquee mechanic — the Golden Age** *(proposal)*: at +20 surplus happiness a
  player may DECLARE a Golden Age: spend 20 happiness → 10 turns of +10% every yield in
  every city. Happiness literally spent, Civ-familiar, and the theme's whole fantasy in
  one button. (An Entry XVII empire-stage percent with a timed effect — every mechanism
  exists.)
- Deeds: ▢ ________

## Æra IV
- Doctrines:
  - The Coronation Games *(proposal)* — completing a wonder, a cathedral or an Opus pillar throws games: +5 happiness in every city for 5 turns.
  - The World's Fair — see 05 (the gold theme's wild card is this theme's crown).
- Deeds:
  - The Most Content *(proposal, reckoning)* — at the close of the age, the empire with the highest surplus happiness.
  - ▢ a Golden-Age race? (first to a second Golden Age?)

Everything past the existing anchors is proposal; the Golden Age needs a ruling before
anything else here matters.
